A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
salvage surgery can be performed with acceptable morbidity and mortality rates, but that survival rates are poor.
salvage laryngectomies following irradiation for carcinoma of the latoro-pharynx should be performed in those cases in which there is no primary recurrence.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of patients with laryngeal carcinoma can be salvaged with a good quality of life following recurrence after radiotherapy.
salvage surgery following radiation failure is a worthwhile procedure.
